coverage.authoredAnalysis: Image-only original cover visually read: PCTE programme of struggle2023-2027 and organisation identity.
Title identifies July2023 and2023-2027 period.

Explicit electoral applicability: programme of opposition to government emerging from23July election; party distinguishes struggle programme from governing electoral platform. Retrospective pandemic/inflation critique and continuation, not independent factual findings.
Retrospective critique completed; why support party and objections to capitalist-party consensus. No use as evidence of opponents individual positions.
Completes consensus critique and refers to separate Manifesto-Programme; current document concretises next-four-year struggle, not automatic incorporation of all other text.

Aspirations1-3: free-choice socially needed employment, progressive workweek reduction never above35hours; at least5weeks paid leave; initial general retirement60 and55 for hard work; worker-controlled/socialised strategic production. Distinguish aspirations from nearer-term section11.

Aspirations4-9: socialised food production/distribution, all available energy sources and sovereignty without named nuclear position, unique public/free/secular in-person education respecting territorial languages, unique public health including psychology/prevention, vacant-home distribution/rehabilitation/building, stable youth life.

Aspirations10-14: equality/socialised reproductive work, free planned sport/culture, peaceful mutual-rights foreign relations, revocable/accountable elected posts and class unity. Socialist planning frame does not establish every specific tax rate.
Organisation and diagnosis of post2008 crisis and social-dialogue structures; introduces current programme of struggle. No additional concrete quantity.

Labour diagnosis with attributed statistics and opposition to flexible work; demands stable full-rights jobs, prohibit temporary-work agencies and barriers to dismissal. No dismissal-compensation day count given.

Immediate workweek reduction without salary loss; no retirement delay and advance with complete State-budget inclusion. Industry oppose relocation/dismantling and State-owned worker-controlled energy firms.
Food-chain minimum producer prices and maximum consumer prices, end Common Agricultural Policy and full farm labour rights. Introduces public-service privatisation critique.

Remove all private firms from education/health/social services; larger staff and no closures especially rural/depopulated places; complete public dental care and needs-based multimodal transport. Separate sectors in questions.

Ban all evictions of working families and basic-supply cuts; access bank/fund vacant homes through uncompensated expropriation; effective rent limits reducing owner gain. No cap amount or precise index instrument. Youth precarity section begins.
Youth critique and opposition to double/triple wage scales and youth-specific precarious contracts; education critique continues16.

Employment status for all practical placements, student representation, betting-shop closure and oppose newly legalised drugs. Women section: reproductive-rights/natality/care and violence diagnosis; source statistics not reused as current facts.

Full reproductive rights and longer birth/care leave; survivor protection/support, equal wages/work and socialised care; prohibit prostitution with integration support and keep surrogacy illegal. Culture/science/sport section begins.

Public free arts/culture/sports facilities and access, stable cultural/research labour conditions and socially directed State science; military-budget/base critique begins. No exact R&D-spending amount.

Unilateral EU/euro exit expressly joined to worker-power installation; unilateral NATO exit, Vatican concordat break, immediate foreign-base closure and prohibit transit for imperialist aggression; stop troops in such missions, not every rescue/peacekeeping operation.

Public-service worker/user/student control, public-post accountability and express revocation right at all levels; worker-controlled public broadcasting. Mere critique of gag-law promise is not an explicit repeal demand here.

Close migrant detention centres, full rights for residents/workers and those fleeing foreign policies, migrant organisation inclusion and oppose racism/xenophobia. No automatic exact citizenship/naturalisation procedure.
Final organisation strategy in workplaces/residential areas/study centres: unions, party units, worker/popular centres and student organisations. Not new electoral-policy instruments.
Completes organisation strategy: worker-women associations, solidarity/peace committees, unilateral UE/NATO departure/base closure and migrant/refugee incorporation. No annex/footnotes follow.
